title: 2006 FIFA World Cup
prose:
The 2006 FIFA World Cup was staged in Germany from 9 June to 9 July, the first edition hosted by a reunified Germany. Leipzig became the first former East German city to host World Cup matches, one of several firsts that gave the tournament its place in the competition's history. Thirty-two teams were drawn into eight groups of four, with the top two from each group advancing to a single-elimination knockout stage spanning the round of 16, quarter-finals, semi-finals, a third-place play-off and the final. Eight nations made their World Cup debuts, including Ghana, Ivory Coast, Togo, Angola, Ukraine, Czech Republic, Trinidad and Tobago, and Serbia and Montenegro. Fittingly for a tournament bookended by defenders, Philipp Lahm opened the competition and Marco Materazzi would later score its decisive equaliser, the first time both the first and last goals of a World Cup came from defenders.

The final pitted Italy against France at Berlin's Olympiastadion. Zinedine Zidane, who won the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player, opened the scoring from a 7th-minute penalty, chipping a Panenka off the crossbar and in. Materazzi equalised in the 19th minute, heading home an Andrea Pirlo corner. The match finished 1–1 after extra time, but its enduring image came late: Zidane was sent off for headbutting Materazzi in the chest, the final act of his playing career.

The contest went to penalties, where Italy prevailed 5–3. France's David Trezeguet was the only player to miss, his kick striking the crossbar, before Fabio Grosso converted the winner to give Italy a fourth World Cup title. France were runners-up, and hosts Germany took third place, beating Portugal 3–1 in the play-off. Germany's Miroslav Klose claimed the Golden Boot with five goals, the lowest tally to top the scoring charts since 1962. The tournament also saw a record number of yellow and red cards issued. Total attendance reached about 3,359,439 across the 64 matches, averaging roughly 52,491 per game.
